title: When the client cries at the scale
bluesky:
When the client cries at the scale

Nobody trains for this part.

https://mojowaylife.com/stories/155-when-the-client-cries-at-the-scale.html
linkedin:
It happens more than the textbooks suggest. A client steps on, sees the number, and something else comes out.

The coach's instinct in that moment is to fix it: reassure, explain, offer a plan. All three are the wrong first move, because none of them address what actually happened, which usually has very little to do with the number.

The number was a permission slip. It let someone feel something they'd been holding for months: a divorce, a diagnosis in the family, a year of being told they'd let themselves go.

What I've seen work is embarrassingly simple. You put the numbers down. You say: we don't have to do this part today. Then you wait, and if they talk, you listen without a plan.

The scan can wait. The relationship can't.

This is the part of coaching work that no tool can do, and also the part where a tool should know when to be quiet.

MOJOWAY's kit produces a page, not a verdict. The coach decides whether today is a data day or a listening day, and the report is patient enough to wait a week.
